title: Add RAG authoring CLI with deterministic replay and artifact packaging
author: Aisha Khanna
release_notes: Add new local-first RAG authoring CLI and packaged artifact format (.ragpkg) for deterministic replay, debugging, and portable quickstarts.
description: Motivation: Teams frequently author RAG flows locally but struggle to reproduce tool-call orderings and debug intermittent failures when moving from dev to CI or private deployments. This PR introduces a lightweight authoring CLI (redwood-rag) that: 1) packages a RAG workspace into a single reproducible artifact (.ragpkg) containing prompt templates, index snapshots (optional), tool stubs, telemetry probes, and a manifest; 2) records a deterministic, stepwise replay log of model calls + tool invocations so runs are reproducible for e2e debugging; 3) provides a minimal sample runner (Python + TS) and a Go micro-runner for embedding in smoke CI and edge sandboxes; 4) ships docs and a quickstart that demonstrates packaging, local replay, snapshot assertion testing, and how to surface stepwise debug traces to the Console. Checklist: - [x] CLI: build, pack, unpack, replay, validate subcommands - [x] .ragpkg format: manifest.json, prompts/, tools/, snapshots/, replay.log - [x] Sample runners: python/ts/go minimal adapters + README - [x] Docs site pages and quickstart tutorial + screenshots - [x] Telemetry probes added to quickstart (step timings, token counts, tool latencies) - [x] Unit tests for packing/unpacking + deterministic replay harness - [x] Smoke e2e in CI against local dev runtime (rerun once due to flakey env) Design notes: The replay log intentionally records non-sensitive metadata only (sha256 of input artifacts, tool IDs, deterministic pseudo-random seeds). Customers must opt in to snapshot uploads in Private deployments; by default snapshots are local-only. The runtime adaptor supports two replay modes: "soft-replay" (re-executes calls but allows different model variant fallbacks) and "strict-replay" (replays exact recorded outputs; useful for debugging aggregator logic). CLI examples: - Pack a workspace: redwood-rag pack ./my-rag-workspace -o my-job.ragpkg - Run local replay (strict): redwood-rag replay --strict my-job.ragpkg - Validate snapshots: redwood-rag validate my-job.ragpkg --assert-prompts
commits: 1) init: scaffold CLI and artifact schema; 2) add: python/ts/go runners and telem probes; 3) docs: quickstart + screenshots; 4) tests: add unit + e2e smoke; 5) fix: address CI flake by pinning local redis for indexing

review_conversation: Ravi: Can we guarantee no sensitive data is included in the .ragpkg by default? Aisha: Yes — the pack command strips known PII keys from local config files and refuses to include files matching patterns in .gitignore unless --force is set. Lucia: The strict-replay mode is helpful but could lull users into false confidence if model determinism differs across hardware. Samir: Add a note in docs describing hardware/model-variant caveats. Aisha: Added opt-in fields and an FAQ section in the docs. Ravi: Approved with comment on expanding telemetry opt-out for private installs. Aisha: Added --no-telem flag and documented KMS/HSM considerations.
ci_summary: CI run 1: lint + unit tests passed, e2e smoke failed with redis bind race; reran smoke after adding ephemeral redis shim. CI run 2: all checks passed (unit, integration, smoke, docs build). Security scan: no high-severity findings; minor TODO to remind users not to check in snapshots. Coverage: pack/unpack ~82%, replay harness ~75%.
testing_notes: Included deterministic test vectors under tests/fixtures/ (seeded PRNG values, small index snapshot, mocked tool outputs). The e2e smoke uses a local dev runtime with a bundled small LLM mock to keep flakiness low. Flaky test encountered in first CI run was due to port conflict on CI runner; fixed by dynamic port allocator.

For Dedicated customers, note that snapshots must be retained within their VPC when used. For Private installer, include --no-telem checkbox in installer UI.
